item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact required API, uses the established multipart helper, preserves FilesOption behavior, and produces a replayable body. B introduces expressly forbidden APIs and retry refactoring.","reasons":["A declares the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption). B substitutes a new AddFileOption type, breaking the specified API.","A uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\" and the supplied filename, yielding the replayable bytes.Reader expected by the retry transport.","B adds multiple association-field options despite the contract explicitly prohibiting association fields.","B changes RawClient retry behavior globally by buffering arbitrary request bodies, contrary to the requirement not to refactor unrelated retry machinery and potentially changing FilesService.Add semantics broadly and silently handling read failures poorly when io.ReadAll fails."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates FilesService.Add request, decoding, and error logic instead of routing the encoded body through Add as explicitly required.","Its tests omit dedicated empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error cases.","The retry test does not visibly set RetryAllMethods to true, making it less faithful to the reported POST-retry scenario."],"risks_b":["Upload has the wrong option type and does not preserve FilesOption behavior.","It adds forbidden association fields and unnecessary NewFileWithFields machinery.","It also duplicates Add rather than routing through it explicitly, despite altering Add indirectly through RawClient.Do globally elsewhere in the stack—violating scope discipline and behavior preservation expectations—and it still omits a source-reader-error test for Upload."]}
